title: Stored Procedures — Basics
description: Learn how to create, execute, modify, and delete stored procedures in SQL Server.

data.text: A stored procedure is a set of Transact-SQL statements stored as a named object in the database. When executed, SQL Server reuses the cached execution plan for fast, reliable performance.

data.title: CREATE PROCEDURE basic example
data.content: Creates a stored procedure that returns a product list.
data.code:
CREATE PROCEDURE uspProductList
AS
BEGIN
    SELECT
        product_name,
        list_price
    FROM
        production.products
    ORDER BY
        product_name;
END;

data.text: You can also use CREATE PROC as a shorthand for CREATE PROCEDURE.

data.title: ALTER PROCEDURE example
data.content: Modifies the stored procedure to sort by list_price instead of product_name.
data.code:
ALTER PROCEDURE uspProductList
AS
BEGIN
    SELECT
        product_name,
        list_price
    FROM
        production.products
    ORDER BY
        list_price;
END;

data.title: DROP PROCEDURE example
data.content: Removes the stored procedure from the database.

data.title: Stored Procedure Basics Key Points
points: Stored procedures group T-SQL statements into reusable named objects.
SQL Server caches execution plans for fast repeated execution.
Use CREATE PROCEDURE to create, ALTER PROCEDURE to modify, and DROP PROCEDURE to delete.
Execute stored procedures using EXECUTE or EXEC.
